title: Python Multiple Assignment Explained: x, y, z = 1, 2, 3
description: There is a way to give x, y and z their values in a single line, and an old way of printing variables with %s and %d that you will still run into in real code, but only one of the two belongs in the code you write.

In this follow-up to my Python variables video I go through x, y, z = 1, 2, 3, the chained x = y = z = 0, and a legacy %s and %d print line, so you know exactly what you are looking at when you meet them.
